psg.note: Tuchel also frequently used a 4-2-2-2; Marquinhos frequently played the deep-midfield role, Neymar worked as a left-sided free creator, and Mbappé operated centrally or from the left. The 4-3-3 is the editorial mapped representative, not a verified modal XI.

marseille.note: Villas-Boas's most common system 4-3-3; Payet primarily LW, Sarr RW, Benedetto centre forward, Sanson/Rongier central. Thauvin had only two brief league appearances and is not in the selected candidate pool.

rennes.note: Stéphan used 4-4-2 with Niang and Hunou as strikers, Raphinha on right and Del Castillo/Tait left, Camavinga plus Bourigeaud central midfield. Raphinha DOB verified independently as December 14, 1996.

lille.note: Galtier paired Osimhen and Rémy in front, André/Sanches in central double pivot and Bamba/Ikoné on opposite wings. André classified as holding DM for site; exact deep-CM match majority to audit. No qualifying league replacement keeper.

nice.note: Vieira changed between 4-3-3 and 4-1-4-1. Danilo deep midfield, Lees-Melou and Cyprien central, Claude-Maurice left and Ounas right in site representative; actual starting eleven varied by injury.

reims.note: Guion 4-2-3-1 approximation: Romao and Chavalerin axis, Cafaro central attacking midfield, Doumbia left, Oudin right (departed in January), Dia striker; post-January lineup changed and original tactical modal not fully independently quantified.

bestXiReview.reason: Best XI in 4-3-3 to preserve genuine individual main positions; Neymar LW, Di Maria RW, Mbappe ST, Marquinhos DM, Verratti/Camavinga CM. 4-2-3-1 league-era dominant variant independently disputed; no fictitious CAM added.
